name: Burst Out Loud
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the
transcription, the rewrite, the card at the foot of the frame, the
palette handed to the user, the highlight that changes FACE and not
colour - all of it is Hall of Femme's and is named here rather than
restated. What makes this show itself is one sentence long: it is set
in Proxima Nova Bold with picked words in Proxima Nova Black, on a
black card, in two colours offered for the type and the same two for
the card.
beauty-hacks is the second pack to read, because it is the one that
already made this move - Hall of Femme's design in Proxima Nova - and
everything about the two cuts of that family is argued out there with
the measurements. This pack differs from it in the palette alone, and
the difference is that there is no brand colour in it.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the packs it was cut from, which
is in the colours and nowhere else. Hall of Femme sets its captions
in Telegraf on a hot pink card; beauty-hacks sets them in Proxima
Nova on a magenta one. This one takes beauty-hacks' type exactly and
reduces the palette to its poles: white and black, offered for the
letters and for the card, opening on white on black.
That makes it the plainest of the packs cut to this design, and
plain is the design rather than the absence of one. Every other one
of them carries a brand colour on the card, which is the shape that
reads first; this one has none to carry, so what reads first is the
contrast itself and the words in it. The card still earns its place -
it is what holds a caption legible over forty unknown photographs,
which is the whole argument for a card, and it is doing that job
alone here rather than doing it while also being the brand.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform text box, the shape of the card, its padding and corners and
shadow, where the block stands on the frame, the drag - is the
Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only what
makes it this show, which is the whole of what a pack under this
heading should be.

_comment_face: Proxima Nova Bold. Which cut that is, why the full name rather
than 'Proxima Nova' is declared, and what the machine may already
know it by are written out in
what capitals at the preset's 40px cost this face, which is
nothing, is written out in beauty-hacks.
The Bold and not the Black, so that a picked word has the heavier
cut to climb into - the argument, and what this pack did before
it, are in beauty-hacks with the measurements.
_comment_color: The channel's own answer, and therefore what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch: a frame stores no colour of its
own until it is given one, and this is what it falls back to (see
state.textColorFor). It is the first of the two in `colors` below,
so the white swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an untouched
frame - though nothing requires that, and the swatch is found by
matching this value rather than by being listed first.
White letters on the black card, which is the strongest pairing
there is: 21 to 1, the full range, with no brand colour in the way
of it. Nothing about this pairing is a compromise between a colour
and its legibility, which is what the note on this key in every
other pack cut to this design is about - here the two questions
have the same answer. Three older packs under this heading already
open on that same 21 to 1 - fight-source and killer-bites on black
like this one, fitness-story-de on white - so the pairing is not
this show's alone, and nothing about it needs to be.
_comment_colors: The two colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and
for the card behind them - two buttons each in the title panel (see
editor.renderColorButtons).
The same two in both lists, which is what every pack under this
heading that offers a palette does, and here it is the whole of the
feature rather than one part of it: the show has no colour to
choose, so what the user is being handed is the DIRECTION. Four
combinations, of which two are a colour on itself and two are the
same 21:1 contrast the opposite way up - white on black for a
caption that sits into a dark still, black on white for one that
cuts out of a bright one. That is a real choice on a grid of forty
frames from one video, and it is the only one this palette makes.
Two rather than the three or four the packs this was cut from
offer. Nothing counts the list - the panel draws a swatch per entry
and the row wraps - so a two-colour row is a two-button row and
costs nothing anywhere. Several packs under this heading offer
exactly two, and fight-source offers these two: the same white and
black, on the same black card, opening the same way round. That is
worth knowing and is not a problem - it is a different show in a
different face, and a palette of the two poles is not a brand
anybody owns.
The two failing combinations are white on white and black on black,
and they are left available for the reason Hall of Femme gives
about precisely them - the two lists are independent because the
pairing is the feature, and a rule barring the matching ones would
cost the panel more explaining than an invisible caption costs a
user who can see it is invisible and presses the other swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note on
`colors` in js/channels.js. This channel's highlight is a different
CUT of the face and not a different colour, so what colour the type
is has one answer and not two.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Proxima Nova Black, in the same colour as
the rest of the block: the highlight is WEIGHT, which is Hall of
Femme's highlight and beauty-hacks' both. That the step climbs -
700 to 900, the way Hall of Femme climbs 200 to 800 - and that a
step this short makes a quiet highlight are measured out in
beauty-hacks, which is where that argument belongs and is not
repeated. This pack ran it the other way round until the seven
shows cut to that design were turned together.
It is worth knowing that this is the pack where that quietness
costs the most. On a magenta card a picked word has the colour of
the card working with it; here there is nothing in the frame but
two weights of one family in one colour, so the 3.2% of set width
between the Bold and the Black is the entire highlight. If this
show ever needs its picked words to carry further, the honest fix
is the one beauty-hacks names - a third cut of the family - rather
than a box, and not a second colour, which would make the
highlight its own question and the palette a different feature.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the face is the whole of the
difference. Stated all the same, for the fallback reason `color`
above is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as
weight would be two highlights.
No shadow stated, so the preset's null stands: these letters are
on a solid card in a colour the user picked, and the card casts
the one shadow there is.
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: Black, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are the
Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the second entry in `colors.panel` above rather than the
first, which is the same freedom every pack under this heading
uses - the swatch that shows as chosen is found by matching this
value and not by being listed first, so both rows can be written in
one order while the channel still opens on white type and a black
The only card among the packs cut to this design that is not a
colour - fight-source and killer-bites are carded in black too,
from a different lineage. It is also the case where the preset's
drop shadow - black at half alpha, 24px of blur, 10px down - is
doing something other than lifting a bright shape off a
photograph: a black card on a dark still would otherwise have no
edge at all, and the blur is the whole of what keeps the rectangle
a rectangle. That is worth knowing before anybody considers
turning the shadow off on this pack in particular.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved - and on this
pack it would be the same colour as the card as well, which is how a
black card ends up with no edge.
